message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
Common examples include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Where you find it |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Skeletal muscle cell (myocyte)** | Contractile muscle fiber | Muscles |
| **Osteoclast** | Bone resorption | Bone tissue |
| **Syncytium** (e.g., placenta, certain viral infections) | Specialized tissue or viral replication | Placenta, infected tissues |
| **Multinucleated giant cell** | Immune response, inflammation | Granulomas, chronic inflammation |

So, if you’re looking for a general term, “multinucleated cell” or “syncytium” is the name. If you need a specific example, skeletal muscle cells and osteoclasts are classic multinucleated cells.
